difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Lemma 3.5 (source0.tex lines 697--718, source label lem: 3.8 extra F), "Let \hat{F}=\sum_{i=1}^m \hat{F}_i and m,\alpha_i,\hat{\beta}_i,\hat{\rho}_i be as in Assumption \ref{ass:critvarsettinglocal}\ref{it:hat F}. Let n\in\R_+, T>0 and \sigma>0. There exist constants M_T,\hat{C}_{n,T},\tilde{C}_{n,T},C_{n,T,\sigma} non-decreasing in T and n, and constants \epsilon_i>0, such that (i) ... (ii) ... (iii) ...", delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 720--762 (43 lines, one adjacent proof environment that opens and closes inside the retained span). The lemma is the technical core of the paper's extension of the critical variational setting to a drift nonlinearity with non-zero \alpha_i: it produces both the growth inequality (i), the local Lipschitz inequality (ii) and, crucially, the sigma-absorbable monotonicity-type bound (iii) on which the paper's continuous-dependence and weak-convergence arguments rest. The proof is complete and self-contained given Assumption 2.1 and Lemma 3.4: it reduces to m=1, chooses the dual pair q=2(\hat{\rho}+1)/(1+2\alpha), q'=2(\hat{\rho}+1)/((1+2\alpha)\hat{\rho}), proves q=\hat{\rho}q'\le 2/(2\hat{\beta}-1) from the \alpha-(sub)criticality condition (1+\hat{\rho}_i)(2\hat{\beta}_i-1)\le 1+2\alpha_i, then chains Hoelder, the critical interpolation estimate of Lemma 3.4 and Young; for part (iii) it invokes the complex-interpolation identities V_\theta=[H,V]_{2\theta-1} and \<y,x\?\le\|y\|_\alpha\|x\|_H^{2\alpha}\|x\|_V^{1-2\alpha}, then uses Young with the dual exponents q=(1+\alpha-\hat{\beta})^{-1}, q'=(-\alpha+\hat{\beta})^{-1} and the bound \hat{\rho}q\le 2/(2\hat{\beta}-1) to absorb \sigma\|u-v\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}^2. That bookkeeping of the subcriticality exponent regime 0\le\alpha_i\le 1/2, \hat{\beta}_i\in(1/2,1], together with the use of complex interpolation of a Gelfand triple, is not a qualifying-exam exercise in unpacking definitions; it is the estimate that fails for supercritical nonlinearities and the reason the paper can treat critical drift terms at all. H2: a complete original research-paper lemma, moderately short, whose argument is a genuine multi-step interpolation-and-absorption chain rather than a routine verification.
